title: Revocable Nobility
spine: Distinguish choosing capable people from granting a finite office, compare unavailable review with permanent audition on one imagined long project, then make independent evidence and reversible public explanation the reasons to read the contract and human coda.

source.scope: Full chapter map and complete existing 20-line film; complete source-3,4,19,38,39,43,50,51,99,100,101,102,103,104,115,123 read. Not the entire book or external reference verification. Table extraction in source-99 and source-39 is visibly scrambled, so statements rely on intact explanatory prose, not reconstructed numerical/table claims.
source.genre: Human-AI institutional inquiry with explicitly normative, conditional simulations; an imaginative proposal, not a ready legal constitution.
source.images: Inspected all 15 non-cover diagrams and charts in review/source-figures.jpg. Adapt conditional office contract and reversible public explanation relationships as enacted situations. Omit literal model plots, rankings and uncertainty bands because the short film does not explain their assumptions sufficiently; no quantitative forecasts are shown.

scenes.title: The office is not the person
lines: Revocable Nobility asks how societies can empower capable leaders without making their offices permanent.
The book proposes temporary, domain-specific authority attached to service and higher accountability.
Selection matters, but its central question concerns the contract that governs whoever wins.
Its human-AI inquiry uses conditional simulations, rather than certifying a rightful ruling class.
Readers examine how correction can remain possible without making difficult leadership impossible.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Respect for difficult service opens into curiosity about a finite mandate; no theatrical villain or hereditary crown.
scenes.artPlan: Open at a modern public-infrastructure planning room overlooking an unfinished pedestrian bridge. A project leader coordinates workers and an actual staged construction plan. A wall-mounted mandate has a visible beginning and ending on a calendar; the leader can leave while the office, archive and unfinished task remain. Keep the project useful and ordinary rather than a palace or tokenized throne. Color identity: copper structural steel, deep indigo plans, pale limestone, bright coral worker equipment and a turquoise landscape. This is an explicitly conceptual infrastructure illustration of the source’s long-project problem, not a named bridge, case study or engineering procedure.

scenes.title: Two ways to lose correction
lines: Imagine a long infrastructure project under two badly designed rules.
Under ceremonial accountability, the leader controls the records used to review that leadership.
The review cannot reliably challenge a warning the institution has made inaccessible.
Under constant removal threats, even an unpopular necessary decision can end the mandate.
The project stalls as leaders protect themselves from every difficult choice.
The source's comparison asks what due process and independent evidence change.
scenes.emotionalPlan: First frustration at blocked scrutiny, then anxiety at permanent audition; neither extreme earns a triumphant verdict.
scenes.artPlan: Use two sequential views of the same unfinished bridge and planning office, not parallel generic icons. First an engineer’s warning is filed in an archive whose only key remains with the incumbent. A reviewer requests it and receives a curated progress picture while the actual warning remains visible behind the office partition. Then reset as a second hypothetical contract: the leader is repeatedly called away from the long work plan to defend each contested step, work crews remain waiting beside unplaced structural sections, and the schedule cannot advance. Do not use a floating bell, empty stamped paper or an invented numerical model chart. The contrast is between unusable review and action-destroying interruption; do not imply every protest or adverse review is illegitimate.

scenes.title: A warning must survive its author
lines: Its proposed contract separates a good-faith error from deliberate concealment.
Warnings survive independently, and review follows conditions declared before the conflict.
The officeholder can answer the evidence instead of facing immediate public punishment.
Power can end while the person retains dignity and ordinary life.
These safeguards remain a research proposal, whose modeled advantages depend on explicit assumptions.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Tension gives way to a usable distinction and humane descent, without celebrating punishment or guaranteeing ideal institutions.
scenes.artPlan: Change to a close independent project archive and review encounter. The engineer deposits the same warning in an independently held record; the incumbent cannot remove it. A pre-existing review condition is consulted, then the officeholder supplies an answer alongside the preserved evidence, rather than receiving an instant guilty stamp. Keep explanation and deliberate destruction of records visually distinct: an attempted missing-page edit cannot alter the retained copy. Show a possible end of mandate through return of the office access badge, while the person takes personal belongings and joins ordinary family or civic life; avoid harm to relatives or confiscating unrelated possessions. Review is explicitly conceptual, not an implemented legal procedure or a declaration that the illustrated leader is guilty. There is no empirical success score.

scenes.title: A public promise you can inspect
lines: Yet citizens have work and families, not unlimited time to inspect institutional complexity.
The book proposes short public commitments that open onto a deeper shared record.
A simplified explanation should lead to sources, responsibility, uncertainty, and a genuine appeal.
Start with The Contract That Selects After Selection, then the final human coda.
Read it to examine how an accountable office could remain both capable and intelligible.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Recognize finite attention without condescension; end with curiosity and the ability to ask a precise question.
scenes.artPlan: Move to an inhabited evening kitchen: an adult balances paid work and care, faced with a deep pile of public project records. A short explanation of the same bridge mandate becomes a usable entry point: selecting its review condition opens the preserved warning and the named independent reviewer, not an unrelated glossy summary. The official and independent views use the same underlying record; no personalized contradictory truth. A clear appeal route reaches another person. Finish with the book’s actual contract chapter and Human Coda, beside the visible record connection; do not transform complexity into a magic one-click consent or completed legal outcome. This adopts the source’s reversible-explanation relationship without copying its statistical charts.

evidence.heading: Author's Note: This Book Is Not Anti-Elite
evidence.quote: Nobility here does not mean hereditary sovereignty. It means a temporary and domain-specific status attached to demanding service and higher accountability.

evidence.heading: Author's Note: This Book Is Not Anti-Elite
evidence.quote: The AI then used historical research and stylized simulations to explore scarcity, surveillance, prosperity, envy, counter-elites, cognitive limits, demographic competition, social fission, and elite selection.

evidence.heading: Method: A Machine That Gives Hints, Not Verdicts
evidence.quote: Charts are examples of model behavior, not measurements of the future.

evidence.heading: The Contract Behind Rank
evidence.quote: The contract proposed here must exist before the crisis.

evidence.heading: The Contract That Selects After Selection
evidence.quote: Instead of asking only who wins office, it asked what the office does to whoever wins.

evidence.heading: The Contract That Selects After Selection
evidence.quote: The officeholder controls appointments, communications, records, and the interpretation of the mandate.

evidence.heading: The Contract That Selects After Selection
evidence.quote: If every unpopular decision can remove the officeholder immediately, leaders optimize for survival, avoid long projects, hide uncertainty, and distribute responsibility until no one can be blamed.

evidence.heading: The Contract That Selects After Selection
evidence.quote: It was that removal needs due process, protected decision space, and predeclared evidence thresholds.

evidence.heading: The Contract That Selects After Selection
evidence.quote: The people investigating cannot depend on the accused for their data, employment, or future jurisdiction.

evidence.heading: The Contract That Selects After Selection
evidence.quote: The contract also distinguishes failure from concealment.

evidence.heading: The Contract That Selects After Selection
evidence.quote: The former officeholder remains a person, may retain recognition for genuine service, and can contribute under a different mandate. Children are not punished for the parent's removal. Property not connected to wrongdoing is not casually confiscated.

evidence.heading: G.7 The Disaster Clause
evidence.quote: This is not ordinary punishment for failure. Good-faith error enters a different pathway and may produce a false-removal cost when institutions react badly.

evidence.heading: G.8 Limits
evidence.quote: The conditional conclusion is not that the simulation found good rulers.

evidence.heading: I.1 The Models Partly Favor the Thesis
evidence.quote: It would be misleading to describe them as neutral competitions among political philosophies.

evidence.heading: The Problem of Government by People Who Have Other Things to Do
evidence.quote: The moral difference is not between a society with theatre and a society without theatre. The difference is between theatre that points toward a common inspectable record and theatre that replaces the record.

evidence.heading: Six Rules and the Right to Ask for the Rest
evidence.quote: The obligation is to create compression that can be reversed.

evidence.heading: Six Rules and the Right to Ask for the Rest
evidence.quote: A citizen should be able to start with a short explanation and travel toward the sources, objections, and consequences without crossing a wall controlled by the speaker.

evidence.heading: Six Rules and the Right to Ask for the Rest
evidence.quote: The institution may adapt language. It may not adapt the constitutional truth.

evidence.heading: A Human Coda: Complexity Is Not Consent
evidence.quote: Most people cannot spend their lives auditing energy systems, demographic dynamics, AI models, constitutional law, fiscal trade-offs, and the hidden incentives of institutions. This is not stupidity. It is the finite condition of human life.

technicalBoundaries: The infrastructure project is explicitly imagined, not a source-reported bridge or engineering example.
No best-ruler certification, calibrated legal threshold, measured social outcome or universal ranking.
Legitimate opposition is not framed as sabotage; the problem is constant removal sensitivity without due process.
Good-faith error, concealed evidence and guilt remain distinct; review includes a defense, not instantaneous punishment.
Loss of office does not confiscate unrelated property or punish family.
A short explanation leads into a shared inspectable record; it does not replace consent or make six rules a cognitive law.
supersedesDefects: Floating bell and blank seal never enacted captured review or long-project timidity.
Repeated methodological qualification displaced the distinctive cognitive-bandwidth problem.
